chunks: Ismaʿil ibn al-Faḍl asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who travels from one land to another, and only stays in his villages and his estate.
So he said: “When you stay in your villages and your land, then complete the salat (prayer); and when you are in other than your land, then shorten it.”

key_terms.يُسَافِرُ: travels from one place to another

ai.seo_question: When should a traveler complete or shorten the prayer if staying on his own land?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about salat (prayer) during travel in relation to a person's own land and property. It states that one completes the prayer when staying in one's own villages or land, and shortens it when in land that is not one's own.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1307 - Ismail ibn al-Fadl asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about a man who travels from one land to another but resides in his own villages and properties.
Imam (as) said: "If you stay in your own village or land, then complete the prayer; if you are in land that is not yours, then shorten the prayer."
